findings.obligation: P8 and E8: acceptance.md S2 P8 expected says a keyboard user can reach every cell, the actions included; handoff falsifier says a keyboard user cannot reach the actions column
findings.observation: Blocking. The keyboard test at line 282 ends after ArrowRight from Name to Owner (line 294). No keystroke moves focus to the actions gridcell, and no assertion checks it. The falsifier for reaching the actions column has no executable observation, which is NEEDS_REVISION under the completeness check.
findings.remediation: Extend the keyboard describe with an ArrowRight from the Owner cell that asserts document.activeElement is the actions gridcell (data-field actions), and that its box is within the 0 to 400 px visible range given by the stand-in geometry. Keep the existing Owner assertions unchanged.

findings.obligation: Test can fail for its own reason: a load error of an existing module must not masquerade as the missing behaviour
findings.observation: Non-blocking for craft, must fix before completion. Line 17 reads ).catch(() => ({})); and swallows every import error, so a horizontalOverflow.ts that exists but fails to load reports none exists yet, the wrong reason.
findings.remediation: Map only module-not-found to undefined and rethrow every other load error, so a broken module fails with its own message.

findings.obligation: Root test rule: test titles name the behaviour, not design ids
findings.observation: Non-blocking. Title begins L3: which is a design obligation id. The same title is copied in acceptance.md S2 Disposition for this test.
findings.remediation: Drop the L3: prefix from the it title and update the matching acceptance.md Disposition row in the same change.

findings.obligation: Browser locator must match the production placement of data-overflow: the host must be a strict ancestor of role grid
findings.observation: Non-blocking, constructibility trap. overflowState filters [data-overflow] by has the table, so only a strict ancestor of the grid matches. Placing data-overflow on the grid element or inside it returns null, and the poll times out with the same symptom as the RED, for the wrong reason.
findings.remediation: Craft places data-overflow on the DataGridBase root Box, which wraps the grid; record that placement in the craft prompt and keep the locator.

findings.obligation: Root rule: keep each check in the lowest layer that can prove it; only what jsdom cannot see belongs in the Playwright spec
findings.observation: Non-blocking. The overflowState polls at lines 58, 77, 114 and 122 assert none, right and left. That state rule is already proven in DataGridBase.overflow.test.tsx and the pure edge test; the browser-only facts are the cue side (sidesWithACue), the table scrolling sideways and the page not scrolling sideways.
findings.remediation: Drop the state polls that jsdom already proves, or keep one settled-state wait justified as a browser settle gate. Keep sidesWithACue, tableScrollsSideways and pageScrollsSideways.

findings.obligation: P6: one decorative shadow shows on the right edge only, a cue shape the design has not declared
findings.observation: Non-blocking. theShownCues at lines 162-167 and sidesWithACue in ReportsListPage.ts count DOM elements with aria-hidden true and pointer-events none. A CSS box-shadow or pseudo-element on the scroller would satisfy the feature and fail the count.
findings.remediation: Design confirms that a DOM overlay element is the cue shape, and records it in feature-delta. If it does not, assert only the data-overflow state in jsdom and keep the browser pixel check.
